body_markdown:
Building apps without coding has become a practical option for founders, small business owners, and teams seeking rapid deployment. Capacity is one platform that helps users create and publish applications through natural-language instructions and connected AI assistants, but it is not the only option for building working apps with managed infrastructure.


An October 2024 forecast estimated the global low-code development platform market at[$28.75 billion for 2024](https://www.marketresearch.com/Fortune-Business-Insights-Pvt-Ltd-v4286/Low-Code-Development-Platform-38425998/) and projected it to reach $264.40 billion by 2032. This guide examines nine Capacity alternatives and complementary tools, starting with[Floot](https://floot.com/) , to help non-technical founders and teams compare app-building features, infrastructure, pricing models, and deployment options.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **Build using existing AI subscriptions** : Floot works with supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. Your AI assistant handles development through[Floot's MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) , subject to client permissions, without a separate Floot AI build-credit charge for standard connector operations.
- **Mobile app development** : iOS and Android builds are available through Floot, with[2 builds per month](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) on Free, 12 on Pro, and unlimited on Power, using Floot's cloud-based building workflows.
- **Managed infrastructure** : Built-in PostgreSQL databases, authentication, hosting, and storage reduce the need to configure and maintain separate infrastructure services.
- **Code ownership and export** : Users own their code and data across all plans, while full project[ZIP export](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) and folder sync require a paid plan.
- **Flexible pricing options** : Free, Pro, and Power plans support different development needs, with separate allowances for building actions, AI features, and hosting.


## **What to Compare When Choosing a Capacity Alternative**


When comparing alternatives to Capacity, consider how each platform supports app development, hosting, and deployment. Modern AI app builders offer different combinations of managed infrastructure, conversational development, visual editing, and integrations. The right choice depends on your project's requirements, technical experience, and budget.


Key factors to evaluate include:


- **AI-assisted development** : Check whether the platform supports natural-language app building, visual editing, or connections to existing AI assistants through MCP.
- **Database and authentication** : Look for built-in databases, user login systems, and persistent data storage for functional applications.
- **Hosting and infrastructure** : Compare managed hosting, storage, custom domains, and deployment capabilities to understand what is included.
- **Mobile app publishing** : Evaluate support for iOS and Android builds, app-store submission workflows, and any associated requirements.
- **Code ownership and flexibility** : Review source-code access, export options, and compatibility with existing development tools.
- **Pricing and usage allowances** : Compare subscription costs, AI credits, building actions, hosting allowances, and potential additional charges.


## **1. Floot**


[Floot](https://floot.com/) is a full-stack app-building platform with an MCP connector that lets users create, edit, and publish applications through supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. Floot is free to start and provides managed infrastructure while the connected AI assistant handles development, with building capabilities depending on the client's connector permissions.


### **Key Features**


- **MCP connector for supported AI assistants** : Build by describing apps in natural language through Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations, subject to connector permissions
- **Managed PostgreSQL database** : Automatic scaling with browser-based table views and SQL access
- **Built-in authentication** : Email/password login plus Google and Microsoft OAuth without separate provider setup
- **File storage with CDN** : Public and private file handling with CDN-backed delivery
- **Mobile app development** : iOS and Android builds supported through[mobile publishing workflows](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot)


### **Plan Options and Pricing**


Floot offers three plans with daily building actions, AI credits for optional features, and hosting allowances. According to its[pricing page](https://floot.com/en/pricing) , the core plan structure is:


- **Free ($0/month)** : Up to 100 building actions per day, with no additional weekly cap,[3,000 one-time signup credits](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/billing-credits-and-plans) , and a one-time $3 hosting credit valid for one year
- **Pro ($25/month)** : 1,000 actions per day, 5,000 monthly AI credits, a $10 monthly hosting allowance, and custom domains
- **Power ($100/month)** : 5,000 actions per day, 15,000 monthly AI credits, and a $25 monthly hosting allowance


Floot's current[mobile documentation](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) lists 2 mobile builds per month on Free, 12 on Pro, and unlimited builds on Power. Failed building actions do not count toward daily allowances, while hosting beyond included amounts uses prepaid credit.


### **Floot's App-Building Advantages**


Floot brings AI-assisted development and managed full-stack infrastructure into one workflow. Users can work through their supported AI assistant while Floot manages the backend services required to run and publish working applications.


- **Existing AI subscriptions** : Standard connector operations use Floot building actions rather than separate Floot AI build credits, although image generation consumes Floot AI credits.
- **Integrated infrastructure** : Managed PostgreSQL, authentication, hosting, storage, and transactional email support applications with user accounts and saved data.
- **External integrations** : Floot's[integration ecosystem](https://floot.com/en/integrations) supports Stripe for payments, PostHog and Google Analytics for tracking, Resend and SendGrid for email, and Zapier for automation.
- **SEO tools** : Optional server-side pre-rendering, page-specific metadata, sitemap.xml, and robots.txt configuration help make published apps accessible to search engines through[SEO settings](https://floot.com/docs/projects/seo) .
- **Mobile workflows** : Floot supports native iOS and Android app builds and testing-track uploads through connected developer accounts.
- **Code and data ownership** : Users own their code, data, and intellectual property on every plan, with database export available across tiers and full project ZIP download on paid plans.


Every Floot plan includes managed PostgreSQL, authentication with Google and Microsoft OAuth, file storage with CDN delivery, and transactional email for testing. Sending email to customers through Floot requires a verified sending domain on a paid plan. Payment processing and app-store publishing may also require separate third-party accounts and fees.


## **2. Lovable**


Lovable, formerly known as GPT Engineer, focuses on generating user interfaces and full-stack web applications through a dedicated platform interface. The platform operates separately from Claude or ChatGPT, using its own AI credits for generation.


### **Primary Focus**


- Full-stack web generation with React and TypeScript apps
- Native backend infrastructure through Lovable Cloud
- PostgreSQL databases with managed hosting
- GitHub sync, including on the Free plan
- Unlimited collaborators across plans


### **App Building Considerations**


Lovable generates visual interfaces and supports demos, prototypes, and full-stack web applications. The platform uses a credit system where debugging and iteration consume credits, with usage varying according to task complexity.


### **Organizational Fit**


Lovable offers a Free plan with 5 daily build credits, up to 30 per month, and unlimited collaborators. The Pro plan costs $25 per month and includes 100 monthly credits and custom domains, while Business starts at $50 per month with SSO, role-based permissions, and additional security controls. The platform serves individuals and teams building web applications through a dedicated AI development interface.


## **3. Bolt.new**


Bolt.new from StackBlitz provides a browser-based IDE approach to AI app building with full code access and GitHub integration.


### **Primary Focus**


- Browser IDE environment with code editing and live preview
- Full code ownership with complete access to generated code
- GitHub sync for version control
- Token-based AI generation
- Bolt Cloud for database, authentication, and hosting


### **App Building Considerations**


Bolt.new is positioned for developers who want code control while using AI assistance. The platform offers npm package access and GitHub integration, making it suitable for technical users who want to maintain standard development workflows.


### **Organizational Fit**


Bolt.new offers a Free plan with 300,000 daily tokens and 1 million monthly tokens. Pro costs $25 per month and includes 10 million monthly tokens with rollover and custom domains. Teams plan starts at $30 per user per month, offering per-member token allowances, centralized billing, and access management. The platform supports individual developers and teams working with browser-based development tools.


## **4. Replit**


Replit is an established cloud IDE platform that has added AI Agent capabilities for code generation and app building.


### **Primary Focus**


- Full development environment with IDE, terminal, and debugging
- Replit Agent for AI-assisted code generation
- PostgreSQL support with database provisioning
- Built-in hosting with custom domain support


### **App Building Considerations**


Replit serves both educational and professional use cases with a full coding environment. The platform offers teaching tools and collaborative features, making it suitable for teams learning to code alongside AI assistance. Usage-based credits mean costs can vary based on development activity.


### **Organizational Fit**


Replit offers a Starter plan with daily Agent usage, a built-in database, and publishing for one live project. Core costs $20 per month, or $18 per month billed annually, with $20 in monthly usage credits. Pro costs $100 per month, or $90 per month billed annually, and includes $100 in monthly credits, up to 15 collaborators, and parallel AI agents. Its development environment supports individual and team-based projects.


## **5. Base44**


Base44 is an AI app builder that was acquired by Wix in June 2025. The platform focuses on fast prototyping with a dedicated interface for app generation.


### **Primary Focus**


- Visual app builder with AI-powered generation
- Integrated database with built-in data storage
- Payment integration with native support
- Managed hosting and deployment


### **App Building Considerations**


Base44 provides a fast path from idea to hosted app with a dedicated interface. Its message-credit and integration-credit allowances are tracked separately, so teams need to evaluate both against their expected building and integration usage.


### **Organizational Fit**


Base44 provides a Free plan with 25 message credits and 100 monthly integration credits. Starter costs $16 per month when billed annually, or $20 monthly, with 100 message credits and 2,000 integration credits. Elite costs $160 per month annually, or $200 monthly, with 1,200 message credits and 50,000 integration credits. These plans accommodate different levels of app-building and integration usage.


## **6. Bubble**


Bubble is a mature visual no-code platform with over a decade of development and a large plugin ecosystem.


### **Primary Focus**


- Visual drag-and-drop builder for design and logic
- Workflow automation for complex business logic
- Extensive plugin marketplace
- Native mobile development support


### **App Building Considerations**


Bubble provides extensive workflow capabilities through its visual interface. Its visual workflow editor can require more hands-on configuration than conversational AI builders, particularly for advanced workflows. Apps are built within Bubble's ecosystem without general source-code export options.


### **Organizational Fit**


Bubble offers a Free plan for development and prototyping. Annual billing starts at $32 per month for Web or $59 for Web + Mobile on Starter. Growth costs $119 or $209 per month, while Team costs $349 or $549 per month for the respective options. The platform supports individuals and organizations developing applications through visual workflows, with pricing varying by deployment type and plan.


## **7. ChatGPT Sites**


ChatGPT Sites lets users create, preview, and publish interactive websites and lightweight applications directly through ChatGPT. It is designed for dashboards, internal tools, resource hubs, and other shareable web experiences.


### **Primary Focus**


- ChatGPT-based building with natural-language instructions
- Managed hosting with shareable URLs
- Database and file storage within supported limits
- Access controls with sharing permissions and sign-in workflows


### **App Building Considerations**


ChatGPT Sites is an option for creating interactive websites and lightweight applications within ChatGPT. It supports persistent data and sign-in features, although available functionality depends on the Sites runtime and account configuration.


Floot provides a different approach through its MCP connector, combining AI-assisted development with managed full-stack infrastructure, payments, and iOS and Android app publishing workflows.


### **Organizational Fit**


ChatGPT Sites is available to eligible ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu users, subject to account and workspace permissions. Creating and editing Sites count toward Codex usage. Hosting is free through December 31, 2026. From January 1, 2027, Plus, Pro, and Business plans include monthly hosting allowances, with charges for usage beyond those allowances. Enterprise billing follows the organization's agreement. Availability, functionality, and usage limits depend on the user's plan and workspace configuration.


## **8. Cursor (Pair with Floot)**


Cursor is an AI-enhanced code editor that pairs with Floot through MCP, combining AI-assisted coding with Floot's managed app infrastructure while maintaining a traditional coding workflow.


### **Primary Focus**


- AI code assistance with intelligent completion and generation
- Codebase understanding with deep context awareness
- MCP connectivity to work with Floot's infrastructure
- Git integration with standard version control


### **App Building Considerations**


Cursor is designed for professional developers who want AI assistance within a familiar coding environment. The tool is complementary to Floot rather than a direct alternative. Through[Floot's MCP integration](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/other-mcp-clients) , developers can use Cursor for code editing while Floot handles database, authentication, backend, and deployment infrastructure.


### **Organizational Fit**


Cursor pricing varies by plan, with free and paid options supporting different AI model access and usage limits. When paired with Floot's remote MCP server, developers can access Floot's project files, database, authentication, backend, and deployment tools while working in their preferred editor, subject to the client's enabled connector permissions.


## **9. Microsoft Power Apps**


Power Apps is Microsoft's enterprise low-code platform integrated with the Microsoft 365 ecosystem.


### **Primary Focus**


- Microsoft 365 integration with SharePoint, Teams, and other services
- Enterprise connectors for business data sources
- Dataverse for managed data platforms
- Governance and compliance with enterprise controls


### **App Building Considerations**


Power Apps serves organizations already invested in the Microsoft ecosystem with requirements for enterprise governance, compliance tracking, and integration with existing Microsoft infrastructure. The platform uses Microsoft licensing and is primarily positioned for business applications within the Microsoft ecosystem.


### **Organizational Fit**


Power Apps offers a free Developer Plan for building and testing applications. As of November 2026, Power Apps Premium costs $20 per user per month with annual billing. However, Microsoft's pricing announcement confirms that the price will increase to $22 per user per month on January 1, 2027. Per-app and pay-as-you-go licensing options are also available through eligible purchasing arrangements, with separate usage and capacity rules.


## **Why Floot Stands Out for Full-Stack Projects**


For non-technical founders and business operators comparing Capacity alternatives,[Floot](https://floot.com/) combines AI-assisted development with managed full-stack infrastructure. Its MCP connector works with supported AI assistants, allowing users to build functional applications without configuring separate backend services.


- **Existing AI subscriptions** : Build through Claude, Codex, Cursor, or compatible ChatGPT configurations using your connected AI assistant, subject to client permissions, without separate Floot AI build-credit charges for standard connector operations.
- **Managed infrastructure** : Get PostgreSQL, authentication, file storage, hosting, and email with[built-in services](https://floot.com/docs/getting-started/how-floot-works) .
- **Defined building allowances** : Use daily action allowances with failed actions excluded, while tracking hosting and optional AI usage separately.
- **Mobile publishing workflows** : Create iOS and Android builds, with[app-store testing](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/publishing-to-app-stores) supported through connected developer accounts.


For MVPs, internal tools, client portals, and customer-facing applications, Floot reduces infrastructure setup while preserving code and data ownership. Paid plans also support project ZIP export and folder sync for teams needing local copies.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What is the primary difference in how Floot and competitors bill for AI usage?**


Floot's MCP connector uses the supported AI assistant's own model access for development, avoiding a separate Floot AI build-credit charge for standard connector operations. Floot meters building actions and hosting separately, while optional features such as its in-app AI agent, image generation, and AI inside published apps can consume Floot AI credits. Capacity also supports building through connected AI subscriptions, while platforms such as Lovable, Bolt.new, and Replit use their own credit or token systems.


### **Does Floot provide a managed backend, and what services are included?**


Yes. Floot includes managed PostgreSQL databases with automatic scaling, user authentication with email/password plus Google and Microsoft OAuth, file storage with CDN-backed delivery, transactional email with sent-message logs, and both web and native push notifications. These services support app development across plans, but[customer email delivery](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/email) requires a verified sending domain on a paid plan, native push requires a connected app-store account, and seven-day database recovery is a paid-plan feature.


### **Can existing code editors like Cursor be used with Floot?**


Yes. Floot provides a remote MCP server that works with Cursor, VS Code, Zed, and other clients supporting Streamable HTTP and OAuth. Developers can connect through the remote endpoint at` https://mcp.floot.com/mcp` to access Floot's project files, database, authentication, backend, and deployment tools while working in their preferred editor, subject to available connector permissions.


### **What are the mobile app building options and requirements with Floot?**


Floot packages web apps into native iOS and Android shells without requiring React Native or Expo. Its[mobile documentation](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) lists 2 builds per month on Free, 12 on Pro, and unlimited builds on Power. Builds run through Floot without requiring a Mac or Xcode when using its cloud publishing workflow. Users need their own developer accounts for app-store submission, connecting Google Play requires a paid Floot plan, and final store approval is not guaranteed.


### **How does Floot's pricing structure accommodate different app development needs?**


Floot offers three tiers under its current pricing: Free provides up to 100 building actions per day, with no additional weekly cap, 3,000 one-time starter AI credits, and a one-time $3 hosting credit valid for one year. Pro at $25 per month includes 1,000 daily actions, 5,000 monthly AI credits, custom domains, and a $10 monthly hosting allowance. Power at $100 per month provides 5,000 daily actions, 15,000 monthly AI credits, and a $25 monthly hosting allowance. Floot's mobile documentation separately lists 2, 12, and unlimited monthly mobile builds across these plans. Annual plans include two months free, while hosting beyond included allowances is billed against prepaid hosting credit.
